newsitem.title: FRANCE: Primakov denies Russia message to Iran on EU row.
newsitem.headline: Primakov denies Russia message to Iran on EU row.

text.p: Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov denied on Monday that he had told Iran its relations with Moscow would not be affected by Tehran's row with the European Union.
"Russia made no statement to Iran on the actions of the EU relating to Iran," he told reporters after meeting EU ministers in Strasbourg.
He said an official statement would be made on Tuesday.

Russia's state-owned Itar-Tass news agency on Sunday quoted Primakov as saying: "Russia is firmly committed to friendly relations with the Islamic Republic of Iran". Tass said the statement was in a message delivered to Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati.

"The recent events...will not effect our Russian-Iranian relations," Tass quoted the message saying. It apparently referred to the row over a German court verdict accusing Iran of ordering the 1992 killings of four Kurdish dissidents in Berlin.
The European Union withdrew its ambassadors after the April 10 German court verdict. EU foreign ministers last week agreed to send the envoys back but suspended ministerial contacts.
Iran's foreign ministry has said it was suspending all talks with the EU, including those affecting human rights, terrorism and chemical and nuclear weapons.

Russia, deeply unhappy about a North Atlantic Treaty Organisation decision to grant membership to some eastern European countries, has made clear it was looking for ways to diversify its foreign policy after the western-dominated first post-Soviet years.
Russian officials have singled out Iran, along with China and India, among the new partners.
